issues.feedback: The spec contradicts itself on execution model: requirements call for running each issue in a subprocess, but Technical Approach says `Orchestrator::run()` in `tokio::spawn`. In-process tasks cannot satisfy persisted PID tracking, cross-process abort, or reliable restart/resume semantics.

`pid: Option<u32>` is described as "OS PID of the tokio task", which is not a real concept. Tokio tasks do not have OS PIDs. If you need PID-based lifecycle/abort from `ralph daemon abort`, you must spawn real child processes (and preferably process groups).

Watching multiple GitHub repos is underspecified against current architecture, which operates on one local workspace/git checkout. Creating fixes and PRs for arbitrary `owner/repo` values is not feasible without a repo-to-local-checkout mapping or clone/worktree management.

`max_concurrent > 1` is not feasible in a single working tree with current orchestrator behavior (branch checkout/merge, file writes, commits). Parallel runs will interfere. Either constrain to `1` or isolate each task in its own git worktree/clone.

Using `project_id = github-<issue-number>` and `abort <issue-number>` is ambiguous across repos and will collide (e.g., issue 42 in two repos). Task identity and CLI abort target must include repo (or a globally unique task ID).

Signal-handling acceptance criterion says in-progress tasks become `pending`, but the feature requires updating GitHub issues to `ralph:paused`. Paused state/label transitions are not defined in task status model or acceptance criteria.

`gh issue list` defaults and label semantics are not fully specified. Without explicit pagination/limit handling, issues can be missed. Also clarify whether configured labels are `ANY` or `ALL` match semantics.

Restart/retry behavior can duplicate comments, labels, and PR creation. Spec needs idempotency rules (e.g., marker in comments, existing-PR detection, safe re-entry for partially completed lifecycle steps).

`tasks.json` mutation from daemon loop, worker completions, and `status/abort` commands is race-prone. Atomic rename alone is not sufficient for concurrent writers; define locking strategy (file lock + in-process mutex) and conflict handling.

Abort flow is incomplete: behavior for stale/nonexistent PID, daemon-not-running, and cleanup of GitHub labels (`in-progress` removal, `aborted` add) is not fully specified. Also define whether abort is best-effort graceful or hard kill after timeout.

`gh pr create` requirements are incomplete: branch/head source, no-diff cases, already-open PRs, and fork/base handling are unspecified. These are common failure modes that affect completion/failed labeling.

The test plan misses mandatory validate conformance coverage for new CLI behavior. Per project rules, new command(s) must have `src/validate/tests_<feature>.rs` and registration in `src/validate/mod.rs`; unit/integration tests alone are insufficient.
